body:
Redline round 2

Reviewed the fix diff from round 1 (34acd12..4c8ed6a), and the coverage pass's candidates over the whole pull request at 4c8ed6a.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 4c8ed6a returned 3 candidates: 3 verified, 0 could not be confirmed, 0 refuted, 0 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 0 already tracked.

Round 1's fixes hold. The placement output is checked before anything is posted, a 422 is recognised when its body has no status, the clone's diff ignores GIT_DIFF_OPTS, and a comment with no path moves into the body again; each fix has a case. The findings left are inputs the new paths assume away: a NUL in a recovered hunk, git attributes that make a text file binary in the clone, a fixture made under the developer's git config, and one temp file made before the scratch folder exists. Nothing in this repository is scheduled or queued against these files, so no overlap applies.

### Correctness (2)

- **R2-1** · correctness · low · confirmed · `scripts/redline-gh.sh:361` · One NUL byte in the recovered hunks makes grep drop every file marker, so every patch-less file's comments go to the body
- **R2-2** · correctness · low · confirmed · `scripts/redline-gh.sh:371` · The clone's pinned git diff still follows git attributes and core.bigFileThreshold, so a text file can come back binary with no hunks

### Other items (2)

- **R2-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `scripts/redline-gh.sh:539` · pr_files makes its temp file before the scratch folder exists, so an interrupt can still leave one behind
- **R2-4** · nit · low · confirmed · `tests/gh-test.sh:173` · The fixture's whole diff follows the developer's git config and GIT_DIFF_OPTS, so the patch-less cases can fail locally

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

comments.body:
**R2-1** · correctness · low · confirmed

**One NUL byte in the recovered hunks makes grep drop every file marker, so every patch-less file's comments go to the body**

The hunks file holds raw diff lines, and three plain `grep $'^@@@redline-file\t'` calls read the file markers out of it: here in recover_hunks (`found`), at 428 in place_comments (`recovered`) and at 720 in post-review (`sourced`). grep treats a file holding a NUL as binary. I checked both halves on this machine. Homebrew gawk keeps a NUL through `{print}` (od shows `-   a  \0   b`), so diff_sections writes it into the hunks file. macOS /usr/bin/awk (20200816) truncates the line at the NUL instead, so the default macOS awk is not exposed. On a file holding `@@@redline-file\tsrc/big.js` and a hunk line with a NUL, the system grep prints `Binary file /tmp/redlinerepro/nul-hunks.txt matches` instead of the marker line, and `cut -f2` passes that line through as a path. GNU grep 3.5 and later prints nothing on stdout and `grep: <file>: binary file matches` on stderr. Either way no real path reaches `found` or `recovered`. In place_comments (lines 433-438) every wanted file therefore gets kind `nopatch` and is not `hunks`, so every comment on every patch-less file in the review, not only the one with the NUL, moves under "The file's patch could not be had from GitHub's listing, its whole diff or this clone". That line is false, because the hunks were found. recover_hunks also sees every file as missing and appends the clone's sections again. `sourced` is empty too, so a later refusal is never acted on. Conditions: a text file over about 100 KiB with a NUL after its first 8,000 bytes, which git's binary check does not look at, so git and the whole diff treat it as text with hunks; a GNU awk or mawk first on PATH (any Linux runner, or gawk installed as awk); and one comment on any patch-less file of that review. What GitHub's listing gives for such a file could not be checked from here.

Proposed fix: Read the markers so a NUL cannot hide them: `grep -a $'^@@@redline-file\t'` at the three sites, or `awk -F'\t' '/^@@@redline-file\t/ {print $2}'`. Add a gh-test case with a NUL past byte 8,000 in a recovered section, run under gawk.

**R2-2** · correctness · low · confirmed

**The clone's pinned git diff still follows git attributes and core.bigFileThreshold, so a text file can come back binary with no hunks**

The command at 371-373 pins the algorithm, the context, the prefixes, renames, `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv`, but not git's decision that a file is binary. That decision comes from attributes, which git reads from the repository's `.gitattributes`, from `.git/info/attributes`, and from `core.attributesFile` (which defaults to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes`, or `~/.config/git/attributes`; git-config(1), lines 3709-3719 of the local man page). It also comes from `core.bigFileThreshold`: files above it "will be treated as if they were labeled binary ... git-diff will not compute diffs" (git-config(1), lines 3662-3667). For a path whose `diff` attribute is unset, git writes `Binary files ... differ` (gitattributes(5), line 843), so its section has no `@@ ` line. diff_sections (line 317) prints a section only from its first `@@ ` line on, so the file gets no hunks and its comments move under the could-not-be-had line, although GitHub would take them inline. A user-level `package-lock.json -diff` or `*.lock binary` is the common case, and lockfiles are among the files over 100 KiB this feature is for. The recover_hunks comment (lines 333-335) and the bash-conventions line this fix diff rewrote both promise that "the user's git configuration and environment cannot move a hunk". The case at gh-test.sh line 483 pins only `diff.*` keys. Conditions: the clone is the source (a pull request over 300 files, or a refused or missing section in the whole diff), and the local attributes or threshold mark a file binary that GitHub treats as text. The guard refuses `git -c` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=` to this role, so I traced this through git's documentation and the code rather than running it. The coverage pass reports a run of it on PR 21: 0 hunks without `--text` and 2 with it.

Proposed fix: Add `--text` to the pinned `git diff`: a wanted file is text by GitHub's listing (`changes` above 0). Add a gh-test case beside the pinned-configuration one, with a global `core.attributesFile` marking `lib/local.txt -diff`, and add `--text` to the pinned flag list in agent-os/standards/scripts/bash-conventions.md.

**R2-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**pr_files makes its temp file before the scratch folder exists, so an interrupt can still leave one behind**

R1-2's fix makes the scratch folder after `all="$(pr_files "$1")"` (place, line 535; post-review, line 706). pr_files makes `redline-gh.XXXXXX` in the real TMPDIR (line 261) and removes it only on its own return paths (lines 265, 269, 272). An interrupt during its paginated `gh api` call, which is the longest read on a large pull request, leaves that file behind. The comment the fix added (lines 536-538 and 707-709) says every temp file of the subcommand is made in the folder the trap removes. The standard it added to bash-conventions.md says a subcommand's temp files, "directly or through the functions it calls", are all made there, "so a failure or an interrupt leaves nothing". The leftover-file cases at gh-test.sh lines 360-365 pass because they fail after pr_files. pr_files' temp file predates this pull request; the claim that covers it is in R1-2's fix.

Proposed fix: Make the scratch folder, set its trap and point TMPDIR at it before `all="$(pr_files "$1")"` in both place and post-review.

**R2-4** · nit · low · confirmed

**The fixture's whole diff follows the developer's git config and GIT_DIFF_OPTS, so the patch-less cases can fail locally**

diff-20.txt, which the shim serves as GitHub's whole diff for PR 20, is made at line 173 with `git -C "$GEN" -c core.quotepath=true diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ -M`. That command does not pin `-U3`, `--diff-algorithm`, `--inter-hunk-context` or `--indent-heuristic`, and it does not unset GIT_DIFF_OPTS. The harness sets neither GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL nor GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM (lines 69-76). So a developer with `diff.context = 0` in their config, or with GIT_DIFF_OPTS=-u0 exported, gets a fixture with no context lines. src/big.js changes at line 100 (line 138), so RIGHT 98 is a context line only under -U3. review-20-text's R1-3 (line 187) then leaves the hunks, and the context-line cases fail. `diff.interHunkContext` merges hunks the same way. The script's own clone diff is pinned (R1-4), so only the fixture is exposed. gen_commit (line 126) also runs under the developer's global config and hooks. CI runs with the default config and is not affected. The guard does not let this role run the harness, so this is traced, not run. The coverage pass reports 3 failures under each setting.

Proposed fix: Make diff-20.txt with the script's pinned flags under `env -u GIT_DIFF_OPTS`, or run every git call of the harness with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and GIT_DIFF_OPTS unset.
